I wrote it the way your lead asked, but a few things are likely to bite, and fixing them doesn't require much more work:

- **Context cost:** With that description, Claude will load the skill for almost any request, and all ~3,000 lines come with it. A question about PTO would pull in the on-call runbook and the code style rules too. That dilutes attention and uses a lot of context.
- **Triggering:** "Use for anything related to our company" gives Claude no signal about when this skill applies versus others, so it may fire too often or be unreliable.
- **Phone numbers:** The org chart's names and phone numbers would be available in every session that triggers the skill. Check that you're comfortable with that, and with the file living in the repo.
- **Maintenance:** A 3,000-line file with 35 alert sections is harder to edit and review than separate files, and merge conflicts are more likely.

If you want to keep "one skill, one place to maintain," a cheap alternative is to keep `company-handbook` as the single skill but make SKILL.md a short index (~40 lines). Put each section in its own file (`code-style.md`, `deploy.md`, `oncall.md`, and so on) in the same folder, and link them from the index with a line on when to read each. Claude then loads only what's relevant. The description would also list the topics (code style, deploys and rollbacks, on-call alerts, PTO/expenses, brand voice, org contacts, glossary). The copy-paste effort is the same, and I can write that version if you'd like.
